stories.title: Maldives president, CDF Munir stress importance of strengthening defence cooperation
summary: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu underscored the importance of strengthening bilateral defence cooperation on Wednesday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

20 MoUs signed Pakistan and the Maldives signed a series of MoUs aimed at deepening bilateral relations in multiple sectors, including defence, IT, cybersecurity, health, education, social protection, agriculture and tourism, among others.
Muizzu, speaking to Dar, “expressed Maldives’ desire to deepen its close relations with Pakistan and explore new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, the FO said.

stories.title: 10 killed, 44 injured as passenger bus overturns on highway in Punjab's Rajanpur
summary: DERA GHAZI KHAN: Ten people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil, Rescue 1122 said.
Later, Umerkot SHO Shakeel Dreshak told Dawn that a case had been registered at his police station, in which the bus driver was also named.
DC Ranjha initially told Dawn that the bus driver had fled the scene after the incident, as well as the bus’s owner.

stories.title: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia sign 'Badr' defence cooperation pact
summary: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia on Wednesday signed a multilateral pact to promote cooperation in defence production and capabilities, the Turkish defence ministry said.

Görgün said in a statement that the accord formed the foundation of a “strategic cooperation” to develop joint production and technology. “Technology sharing, joint development and strengthening domestic production capabilities lie at the heart of sustainable defence industry.

During his November 2025 visit to the Gulf state, President Asif Ali Zardari met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and offered to expand bilateral cooperation in the areas of defence production.

stories.title: Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble
summary: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.
Wiz said it coordinated with the PHP team, OpenAI, and the cybersecurity company Calif on the discovery of the vulnerability and patch verification.

A screen displays the unavailable French government website, info.gouv.fr, as cyber agencies warn that websites may be taken offline while PHP prepares a critical fix, in Berlin, Germany on October 21, 2026. — Reuters

stories.title: LHC moved for release of Imran's sisters as 30-day detention period ends
summary: LAHORE: The son of Aleema Khan, detained sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, moved the Lahore High Court (LHC) on Wednesday, seeking the production and release of his mother, as well as two aunts.
Aleema’s son, Shahrez Khan, filed a fresh plea challenging their detention in the LHC on Wednesday.
The petition stated that Imran’s sisters remained at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail despite the lapse of the 30-day period of their detention.

stories.title: Senate body summons ASF official over alleged mistreatment of passengers at airports
summary: Taking up a privilege motion moved by Senator Zehri concerning the alleged inappropriate conduct of ASF personnel, the committee reviewed the response received regarding an inquiry report that it had sought last month.

The committee had taken up the privilege motion by Senator Zehri in a previous meeting on Sept 11, regarding alleged misbehaviour by ASF officials during a check-in for Emirates flight EK-601 on July 24.

According to the motion, a copy of which is available with Dawn, Senator Butt alleged a breach of her privilege and that of the Senate and its standing committee arising out of the conduct of the vice chancellor in connection with proceedings relating to matters concerning PIFD.

stories.title: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in alleged CCD encounter
summary: The suspect accused of running over and fatally injuring a 14-year-old boy in Multan was killed in an alleged encounter with the Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur early on Wednesday, police said.
A Multan court on Tuesday granted police three-day physical remand of the suspect.
On Tuesday, police requested a 14-day physical remand of the suspect for investigation.

stories.title: PHC orders provisional de-sealing of KP Assembly deputy speaker's official residence
summary: The counsel further said that under Section 20 of the KP Provincial Assembly Speaker and Deputy Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975, Bibi was entitled to a “fully furnished official residence” in Peshawar for her “entire tenure as the deputy speaker”.

The lawyer claimed that following the imposition of governor’s rule on Oct 11, police, “without any reason and justification”, raided Bibi’s official residence to “harass her and illegally and unlawfully arrest her”.

She requested the court to direct the relevant respondents, including the provincial government and the KP IG, to “immediately” de-seal the premises and restore the her lawful access and possession to the official residence.

stories.title: Suspect should not be deprived of bail in case of 'reasonable doubt' over involvement, SC rules
summary: ISLAMABAD: Taking exception to the prosecution’s shifting stance without realising the gravity of that conduct in a case regarding expired drugs, the Supreme Court has ruled that whenever reasonable doubt arises, a suspect should not be deprived of the benefit of bail.

Based on these sections, a two-judge SC bench on April 16 granted post-arrest bail to the petitioner on furnishing bail bonds to the tune of Rs100,000 with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.

When the SC’s bail order was sent for compliance, it emerged that the prosecution modified the first information report (FIR) by replacing the original provisions with Sections 409, 471, 468, 467, 420, 109 of PPC, read with Section 5 (2) of the 1947 Prevention of Corruption Act.

stories.title: Apple will have limited iPhone Duo units available in stores on Friday
summary: Apple on Wednesday said it will have ‘limited’ numbers of its folding iPhone Duo phone available for walk-in customers when the device launches on Friday, after initial online orders sold out in minutes and pushed delivery times for some customers to January.

Other regions will only have iPhone Duo units available for customers who already bought them online, including mainland China, France, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the UAE, Apple said.
On the China-governed island of Macau, the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers only, with limited inventory, Apple said.

stories.title: Pakistani who allegedly defrauded US Postal Service remanded in NCCIA Lahore's custody
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Wednesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) five-day physical remand of a suspect in an alleged Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage labels.

The NCCIA’s Lahore zone announced his arrest at a press conference a day ago, saying that the suspect operated a website to market and sell over 5m fake postage stamps over a period of more than three years.
The agency’s investigating officer told the court that the suspect had allegedly been operating a website, LabelsBank.com, since August 2023 to sell more than 5m counterfeit postage labels.

stories.title: ATC appoints state counsel for Imaan, Hadi in security breach case
summary: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Wednesday appointed a state counsel to cross-examine prosecution witnesses from the defence side in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha.

He had shown up in the Islamabad district and sessions court during a November hearing instead of Advocate Shakeel Jatt, the state counsel who was initially appointed to represent the duo in the case.

Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president.

stories.title: JI announces third wave of anti-levy protests across country on Friday
summary: LAHORE: The Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) announced on Wednesday that it will launch the third phase of its nationwide protest movement against the petroleum levy on Friday, with sit-ins planned in all districts across the country, according to a press release by the party.

Wednesday’s press release by JI said the new phase of demonstrations would begin on the instructions of party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, and that the party’s clear and firm demand remained the complete abolition of the petroleum levy.
On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

stories.title: Monitoring the monitors: US states prepare for surge of Justice Dept election watchers
summary: Some state and local laws allow election officials to prevent DOJ monitors from being present inside polling locations.
DOJ staff can observe voting, speak to voters after they leave polling places and report immediate concerns to local law enforcement or election officials.
Two Minnesota counties, Hennepin and Ramsey, invoked state law to keep DOJ monitors from within 30 metres of polling places during the primary election in August.

stories.title: ‘Where are the courts?’: Killing of Multan suspect in alleged CCD encounter sparks concern among lawyers, journalists
summary: The death of a suspect, allegedly during an exchange of fire with Punjab’s Crime Control Department (CCD), sparked questions from lawyers and journalists on Wednesday regarding extrajudicial killings and due process.
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) alleged earlier this year that the CCD has adopted a “deliberate policy of staged police encounters leading to extrajudicial killings”.

Journalist Maryam Nawaz Khan termed it a “total failure of the system”. “When the state relies solely on CCD or police encounters, it’s an admission that our judicial system is dead,” she contended while commenting on Butt’s post.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs2.71, increases diesel by 31 paisas for Oct 22
summary: The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.71 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 31 paisas per litre for October 22.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs379.31 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs390.11 per litre for Thursday.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

stories.title: Pakistan's mythologised idea of an all-rounder finds a home in Arafat Minhas
summary: Arafat makes it look innate, even though it is anything but.
What was particularly remarkable about Arafat during the game was that he managed to take Pakistan out of situations that normally result in the team sinking further down.

Pakistan had a disappointing show last time out in India, but what was particularly disappointing was how the team’s spin arsenal fared even in favourable conditions — a dire set of sporting circumstances that culminated in the team’s first ever ODI loss to Afghanistan.

stories.title: Child protection bureau takes 16 children into protective custody following Multan incident
summary: Punjab's Child Protection and Welfare Bureau (CPWB) on Wednesday took 16 minor children residing at an orphanage in Multan into protective custody and shifted them to the bureau’s Multan centre following a recent incident in the city.
On the directives of CPWB Chairperson Sarah Ahmed, a bureau team visited the orphanage and transferred the children to ensure their safety and proper care.
The bureau had written to the commission to review the orphanage’s registration and take necessary action in accordance with the law.

stories.title: Macron takes aim at Trump for using France riots for election gain
summary: President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday took an apparent swipe at counterpart Donald Trump of exploiting France’s riots for advantage in the US midterm election battle, as Paris prepared for more protests this weekend.
France’s government has admitted it “lost control” in the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings.
Since the rioting — the worst France has seen in years — and ahead of further cost-of-living demonstrations this coming Saturday, Macron’s government has warned it will brook no further violence.

stories.title: Task force seeks guaranteed funding, direct polls for local govts
summary: A task force on local governance on Wednesday called for constitutionally guaranteed funding, directly elected mayors and stronger safeguards for local councils, warning that provincial political and bureaucratic control has undermined devolution of power in Pakistan.
Punjab law draws criticism The report criticised the Punjab Local Government Act 2025 for retaining provincial executive control over elected councils.

Constitutional safeguards The report proposed expanding Article 140-A through a constitutional schedule defining local government responsibilities, including education, healthcare and municipal services.

stories.title: Egypt's Sisi says Saudi defence role would not include attack on Yemen
summary: On Monday, Egypt's parliament ​delayed until October 26 a vote ​on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, lawmakers said, extending ​deliberations over a potentially deeper ​Egyptian role following recent attacks by Yemen's ‌Houthis.
Read: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked Sisi added that Egypt's support for Gulf states was an ⁠extension ​of shared Arab national ​security.
The statement came days after the Egyptian president said last week that Cairo would take all necessary measures to defend Saudi Arabia if requested, amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom.

stories.title: 17 sugar mill workers remain missing after abduction in K-P's DI Khan
summary: At least 17 sugar mill workers remained missing after unidentified armed men abducted passengers and workers from a passenger coach and a sugar mill bus near Cheera Minor on the Indus Highway in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Dera Ismail Khan, while several passengers have been released.
Armed men intercepted a coach travelling from Dera Ghazi Khan to Rawalpindi and took several passengers away.

Read: Armed men abduct 20 trainee police personnel travelling from Kalat to Nushki: officials However, 17 workers of the sugar mills remained missing, prompting residents to take to the streets and block traffic on the Indus Highway in protest.

stories.title: PHC stays arrest of K-P Assembly deputy speaker, orders de-sealing of official residence
summary: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Wednesday restrained the police from arresting Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Deputy Speaker Suraiya Bibi under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance and suspended the administration’s notification sealing her official residence.
Counsel for the petitioner told the court that Suraiya Bibi was allotted the official residence in 2024 in her capacity as deputy speaker.

Read: K-P speaker, deputy set for enhanced privileges Khattak argued that even under emergency and Governor’s Rule, the official residence of the deputy speaker could not be sealed without fulfilling legal requirements.

stories.title: Waseem Abbas case: HRCP calls for independent probe after alleged extrajudicial killing of prime suspect
summary: The report stated that Abbas had fled to a neighbouring street to escape the alleged abuse, while the two suspects pursued him in a vehicle.
The FIR alleged that the suspects ran the vehicle over Abbas with the intention of killing him.
According to the report, they told police that Abbas had passed by shortly before the incident, saying that the suspects wanted to kill him and that he was running to save his life.

stories.title: Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain
summary: The first Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain, which is behind a major DR Congo outbreak, and the patient is a diplomat, an emergency meeting heard on Wednesday.

The case in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda to the capital Abuja on Oct 3, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) also confirmed that it was the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. “This person is actually a diplomat,” another official said, adding the patient has deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”.

stories.title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT ads to Pakistan and 25 more countries in bid to boost revenue
summary: OpenAI said on Wednesday it was expanding advertising on ChatGPT to Pakistan and 25 additional countries, bringing the total number of markets where ads are available to 89, as the artificial intelligence company seeks to grow revenue ahead of a potential initial public offering.
OpenAI began testing ads on ChatGPT's Free and Go plans in the United States earlier this year.
Advertisers can access ChatGPT ads in the new markets through technology partners or use a self-service option through the company's Ads Manager platform.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral visuals do not show Bangladeshi man, woman executed in Saudi Arabia
summary: Another Indian user, based on its past posts, shared the same clip with the following caption: “Saudi Arabia executes two Bangladeshi nationals over ‘having sex’ inside Makkah Mosque.

An Indian account shared the same video, on the same day, with the caption: “A little Bangladeshi girl places soil on the graves of her mother and father following their execution in Saudi Arabia over an alleged act inside a mosque in Makkah.” The post received 681,700 views.

A Thai account also shared the same footage with a caption in Thai that reads: “A Bangladeshi couple were on their honeymoon trip for Umrah when a Pakistani man secretly filmed them kissing in a mosque courtyard and sent the video to Saudi Arabian authorities.

stories.title: Gulf states hold extraordinary meeting in Riyadh to boost military coordination, readiness
summary: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states held an extraordinary meeting in Riyadh on Wednesday to discuss strengthening cooperation and coordination among their armed forces amid continued attacks by Yemen’s Houthi group on Saudi Arabia.
The meeting was held by the GCC Armed Forces Operations and Training Committee, according to a statement from the UAE Defence Ministry.
The meeting comes amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Houthi group on Saudi Arabia and Gulf and international efforts to halt them.

stories.title: PTI dismisses reports of internal rifts as Dogar signals possible resumption of talks with government
summary: He expressed full confidence in opposition leaders Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, saying they had been entrusted with responsibilities by the party’s founding chairman and that party members were expected to support them.

A narrative is being spread that 68 members of the K-P Assembly are set to announce the provincial president and the candidate for the next Chief Minister as a group without the permission of Imran Khan sahib and the party's Political Committee,” he stated on X.
In his absence, the province's General Secretary Ali Asghar Khan sahib is the acting president.” Raja also maintained that Afridi remained the chief minister under the Constitution and the law.

stories.title: US envoy to meet Putin after 'positive' talks with Zelensky
summary: Washington’s envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Saint Petersburg early Wednesday to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin following what US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine.
After talks with Witkoff in Oslo, Zelensky thanked Washington on Tuesday for the resumption of US intelligence sharing on Russian strikes.
Trump has also been keeping up the pressure on Ukraine, saying at the White House that he wanted Zelensky to “make a deal” with Russia, which is ramping up its strikes as a bitter winter looms.

stories.title: Haider Ali snares silver in Nagoya
summary: Pakistan's premier athlete Haider Ali won silver in the men's F37 discus throw event at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya, Japan, on Wednesday, finishing behind Uzbekistan's Kudratillokhon Marufkhujaev in a closely contested final.
Ali, who won gold in the discus throw at the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games, recorded a throw of 57.20 metres to secure second place in Nagoya.
He won gold in the discus throw at the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games, silver in the long jump at Beijing 2008 and bronze in the long jump at Rio 2016.

stories.title: End of an era? How the Hermes Birkin bag is losing its scarcity appeal
summary: Resale market under pressure Managing Director of Lilac Blue Antoinette Hunter unboxes a 2025 Birkin bag in the shade of peppermint at the Knightsbridge private Hermes resale boutique in London, Britain, October 19, 2026.
Business model under scrutinty Hermes Birkin bags are displayed at London Bear, an exclusive boutique for authenticated pre-owned luxury fashion, in London, Britain, October 19, 2026.

For more than a decade, limited supply and strong demand allowed Birkins to command hefty resale premiums, benefiting both Hermes and resellers as the prospects of making a profit via the secondary market encouraged Hermes clients to buy more from the brand.

stories.title: Authors urge UK to halt 'draconian' Palestine Action ban as Rooney sales end
summary: More than 150 writers and personalities signed an open letter Wednesday urging the UK government to amend its "draconian" ban on Palestine Action after Irish author Sally Rooney said she was halting book sales in Britain as a result.

The Labour government has been heavily criticised by some for proscribing Palestine Action as a "terrorist" group in July 2025, with thousands of people arrested since for protesting against the move.
Rooney has repeatedly expressed her support for Palestine Action and said she intends to fund the group, which is not proscribed by Ireland, where the author lives and works.

stories.title: Tesla-SpaceX deal: Wall St says inevitable but Musk says it's not certain
summary: Elon Musk sees "a lot of merit" in combining Tesla and SpaceX, but the decision is ​not his to make: two special committees he cannot join and a Tesla shareholder vote he calls a high hurdle ‌stand in the way.
Tesla's vote is the hurdle Control may also be part of Musk's appeal for a merger.
Musk holds about 85% of SpaceX's voting power through super-voting shares. ‌But ⁠at Tesla he has roughly 20%.

stories.title: ECP orders fresh schedule for Islamabad local government polls
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday directed its office to prepare and issue the election programme for local government elections in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT).

The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday ruled that Islamabad local government (LG) elections would be conducted under the ICT Local Government Act, 2015, adding that it would issue a schedule for the polls later in the day.

Raja further told the hearing that the interior minister, interior secretary and the chief commissioner, on behalf of the ministerial committee, had provided an undertaking. “It appears that the government does not wish to hold local government elections in Islamabad,” he said.

stories.title: Sarmad Khoosat calls for royalties as ‘Humsafar’ prepares for Spanish-language release
summary: Pakistan's television industry, however, has long struggled with the absence of a consistent royalty system.
The practice was discontinued in the 1990s, when several prominent actors reportedly agreed to give up royalty rights in exchange for higher payments from the state-run Pakistan Television (PTV).

For Khoosat, the international expansion of a drama remains a milestone, but the absence of royalties highlights a longstanding gap between the global reach of Pakistani entertainment and the financial protections available to the people behind it.

stories.title: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that companies ​building data centres should pay a "dividend" to the communities ‌where they are sited if they want to make the developments popular.

"I have watched the process closely, and data centres that were highly unpopular in ​a certain area have become extremely popular when a ​financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social ⁠post.
Trump said in February that major technology companies must build their own power plants for their data centres in ​order to protect ​consumers from rising ⁠bills.

stories.title: Aijaz Aslam shares thought-provoking message on society normalising sin
summary: Pakistani actor Aijaz Aslam sparked reflection on social attitudes after sharing a message about how certain behaviours can become so common that people stop questioning their moral implications.

The actor took to Instagram to share a thought-provoking post highlighting everyday terms such as “Drink,” “Date,” “Chai Pani,” “Interest,” “Fashion” and “Friendship,” alongside Urdu references that question how society views such practices.
Alongside his reflective post, Aijaz has also shared an emotional update about his professional journey, offering followers a glimpse into the closing moments of Pehlī Baarish.

stories.title: Pakistani celebrities react as death of 15-year-old Waseem Abbas in Multan sparks calls for justice
summary: Among the celebrities reacting to Waseem's death was actor Yumna Zaidi, who shared a response on her Instagram stories as news of the incident spread.

The circumstances of Waseem's case have also prompted questions about how children are selected for placements, whether their working conditions are monitored and what procedures exist for responding when a child reports mistreatment or attempts to leave a workplace.
Police have said they are investigating the case, including the roles of the suspects and the circumstances surrounding Waseem's placement.
